assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation turned the ubiquitin-proteasome system into a designable chemical tool. Bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues give precise, rational control over molecular recognition and make 'undruggable' proteins addressable. It has changed what chemists and clinicians can do, and has spread across chemical biology and drug discovery.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies (with Sakamoto) introduced the PROTAC concept and first proofs; Ciulli provided structure-guided design and VHL ligands. The glue branch (Handa, Ito on cereblon; thalidomide mechanism) is a separate strand and credit is crowded. Three-laureate set of Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli is plausible but Sakamoto and the cereblon work could be argued.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in late-stage trials and the mechanism is well confirmed by many independent groups. Timing is good, though approval of a PROTAC drug is still pending.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants PROTACs and molecular glues combined or separated
Weight of Sakamoto and the cereblon/thalidomide discoveries is uncertain to me
Clinical validation not yet complete (my recollection)

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Site-specific incorporation of noncanonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs gives chemists atomic-level control over protein composition in living cells. It is a general, widely used platform for probes, crosslinkers, photoswitches and biotherapeutics, and a clear design principle for programmable biomolecules.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first in vivo methods, Chin extended them to eukaryotes, multiple codons and genome-recoded organisms. Mehl and Yokoyama contributed key enzymes and systems. Schultz, Chin and Wang is a defensible trio, though ordering of contributions is disputable.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent use, with robust, stable methodology and active extension (recoded genomes). Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Relative credit among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama
Efficiency limits in multi-site incorporation in higher organisms

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one base to another on DNA without double-strand cleavage, using engineered deaminases fused to Cas proteins. This is molecular design with direct therapeutic consequences, and clinical trials and first patient treatments have begun. It extends the CRISPR recognition of 2020 with a distinctly chemical approach.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual driver; Komor and Gaudelli were lead trainees, and Nishida and Kondo made an independent cytidine-deaminase variant. A sole-laureate configuration is cleanest, but the independent Japanese work leaves a minor allocation question.
assessment.maturity: Rapid adoption and early clinical proof, though long-term safety and durability remain under study. Somewhat early, but strongly supported by many independent labs.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees base editing as too close to the 2020 CRISPR prize
Independent contribution of Nishida and Kondo

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The concept that liquid-liquid phase separation organizes cellular biochemistry via condensates reshaped how chemists think about cell compartments, weak multivalent interactions and self-assembly of peptides and proteins. It strongly resonates with my own peptide-assembly interests and with Sparr's field.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman made the 2009 P-granule discovery; Rosen supplied the multivalent-interaction chemistry framework; Pappu and Mittag contributed physical theory. Pairing is plausible but the field has several essential contributors.
assessment.maturity: Highly cited and broadly adopted, but debate continues about physiological relevance, definitions and artefacts. Some of the interpretation may still be unsettled.
uncertainties: Controversy over in vivo relevance and the term 'phase separation'
Fair allocation among five or more key contributors
May be seen as more cell biology than chemistry

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry for siRNA and mRNA drugs, including COVID-19 vaccines. Design of pH-responsive lipids to encapsulate and release nucleic acids is chemical design with enormous documented societal impact, a rare case of direct translation at global scale.
assessment.attribution: Cullis, Hope, Madden and MacLachlan developed the core LNP and ionizable-lipid technology; Anderson and Langer contributed combinatorial lipid design. The credit is dispersed and contested between academic and industrial contributors.
assessment.maturity: Impact is proven in large populations. The 2023 Medicine prize recognized the nucleoside modification, so the delivery side is a logical complement.
uncertainties: Complex credit and patent-related disputes among contributors
Overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize may weigh on the committee

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing makes single molecules electrically readable and has produced commercial long-read DNA/RNA sequencers and a general platform for single-molecule analysis. It combines protein engineering, chemistry and physics, and it is exactly the kind of sensor technology that spreads across biomedicine.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz proposed and demonstrated early translocation; Bayley engineered alpha-hemolysin pores and covalent chemistry; Akeson led the enzyme-controlled DNA movement that made sequencing practical. Choosing three of five is difficult and Branton's death may constrain things.
assessment.maturity: Technology is widely used and mature, with sequencing a commercial reality. Recognition is timely, but the invention is distributed.
uncertainties: Attribution among five founders, with Branton possibly deceased and ineligible
Overlap with the sequencing field if the committee prefers B001

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based probes report functional state of enzymes in complex proteomes and led to inhibitor discovery and ligandable-cysteine mapping. It is a design-based chemical tool that changed how enzymes are studied in disease, and it is highly relevant for chemical biology and bioanalytical work.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt is the central originator and advocate of the ABPP platform; Bogyo and Overkleeft developed probes for specific enzyme classes, Weerapana contributed cysteine profiling. A one or two-person prize seems realistic.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely used, and with expanding clinical-stage compounds from chemoproteomics. Timeliness is reasonable.
uncertainties: Whether to include Bogyo or Overkleeft alongside Cravatt
Impact may be seen as methodological rather than conceptual

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation lets chemists assemble whole proteins from synthetic peptides and enables protein semisynthesis with modifications, probes and unnatural residues. It provides atomic precision in protein design, and is conceptually elegant and broadly practiced.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson with colleagues introduced native chemical ligation in 1994; Muir developed expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis. Danishefsky made major related contributions. A trio is plausible but the allocation is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent confirmation make this very mature, perhaps a long-overdue candidate rather than a premature one.
uncertainties: Competing claims of Danishefsky, Brik and Liu
Impact on biomedicine is less direct than for newer therapeutic chemistries
